Peter has a 1200-page book published in the 19th century. He uses a scanner to scan the books into a collection of image files, then converts the image files into text files by optical character recognition (OCR). Which of the following are the major benefits of this action?Peter can share the book with ease by uploading the image files on the internet.Peter can search for text in the book with ease.Peter can discard the book to save storage space.(1) and (2) only(1) and (3) only(2) and (3) only(1), (2) and (3)1023.6

AnalysisFor item (1), it takes more time to share a book by transferring the physical copy between readers. Moreover, the book risks being damaged in the process. Therefore, being able to share the book in a digital form is a major benefit.For item (2), manually searching for text in a 1200-page book is very time-consuming but searching for text in an electronic document can be done fast and correctly by a computer. Therefore, the support of easy searching is a major benefit.For item (3), sometimes, the physical copy will be discarded after digitalisation for saving storage space. However, it is not a must. In this case, a book published in the 19th century is a valuable resource and is thus worth keeping.SolutionThe answer is A.1033.6

A computer uses 4-bit two’s complement representation to store integers. Which of the following calculations involves an overflow error? 2 − 3 + 4 − 23 + 4 + 2 − 22 + 3 − 4 − 2−2 − 3 – 3603.3

AnalysisThe range of a 4-bit two’s complement representation is from −24−1 to 24−1−1, i.e. from −8 to 7.For option A, 2 − 3 + 4 − 2 = −1 + 4 − 2 = 3 − 2 = 1. No result is out of range.For option B, 3 + 4 + 2 − 2 = 7 + 2 − 2 = 9 − 2 = 7. Although the final result is not out of range, a number which is out of range appears in the calculation, meaning that an overflow error occurs during the calculation.For option C, 2 + 3 − 4 − 2 = 5 − 4 − 2 = 1 − 2 = −1. No result is out of range.For option D, −2 − 3 − 3 = −5 − 3 = −8. No result is out of range.Only option B involves an overflow error.SolutionThe answer is B.613.3

Jane’s computer uses 8-bit two’s complement representation to store numbers. She increments a number X by 3, then an overflow error occurs. What is the number X?0111 11101111 11100000 11011000 0000623.3

Analysis3 is a positive number. Overflow error occurs only if two numbers of the same sign are added together. The representations of option B and D both represent a negative number. Therefore, option B and D cannot be the answer. The 8-bit two’s complement representation of 3 is 0000 0011. For option A, 0111 1110 represents a positive number. 0111 1110 + 0000 0011 = 1000 0001, which represents a negative number. For option C, 0000 1101 represents a positive number. 0000 1101 + 0000 0011 = 0001 0000, which represents a positive number.SolutionThe answer is A.633.3

Assume that P, Q and R are all 3-bit unsigned integers, under what conditions would an overflow error occur during this calculation?P = 7P > RP > 3 and Q > 4(1) and (2) only(1) and (3) only(2) and (3) only(1), (2) and (3)643.3

AnalysisFor item (1), if Q = 0, then P + Q = 7, which is NOT out of the range of a 3-bit unsigned integer.For item (2), since P, Q and R are all unsigned integers, they can only be zero or positive. Adding zero or a positive integer to P should result in an integer larger than P.For item (3), if P > 3 and Q > 4, then P + Q > 7. A 3-bit unsigned integer cannot be larger than 7.SolutionThe answer is C.653.3
